title: pybind11 error during subscription take_message() when message has NaN value
body:
## Bug report

**Required Info:**

- Operating System:
  - Ubuntu 20.04
- Installation type:
  - binaries or from source
- Version or commit hash:
  - 77949d2c54b8104e48a94d0ea83c7049e18a8809
- DDS implementation:
  - I've tried rmw_fastrtps_cpp and rmw_cyclonedds
- Client library (if applicable):
  - rclpy

#### Steps to reproduce issue

1. Clone [nan_publisher](https://github.com/jacobperron/nan_publisher) to a workspace and build it.
2. Source the workspace and run the publisher. It will publish nan values to a topic `/nan`:

        ros2 run nan_publisher nan_publisher
3. Try to echo the `/nan` topic (e.g. with `ros2topic`):

        ros2 topic echo /nan

#### Expected behavior

The subscriber does not crash.

#### Actual behavior

The subscriber crashes with the following message:

```
make_tuple(): unable to convert argument of type 'object' to Python object
```
#### Additional information

The following line is failing, because (I think) `pytaken_msg` is not initialized:

https://github.com/ros2/rclpy/blob/77949d2c54b8104e48a94d0ea83c7049e18a8809/rclpy/src/rclpy/subscription.cpp#L130-L133

I've added some print statements to that file and can confirm that `pytaken_msg` evaluates to false, e.g.

```diff
+  if (!pytaken_msg) {
+    std::cerr << "We see this print statement" << std::endl;
+  }
+
   return py::make_tuple(
```

I don't know _why_ `pytaken_msg` evaluates to false, but I suppose it has to do with the message failing to be converted into Python.
